# CapStack

> CapStack models real-estate capital stacks: senior debt, LIHTC & historic tax credits, grants, soft loans, deferred developer fee, and equity — see your financing gap, blended cost, stacking conflicts, and the order to secure each source.

CapStack is a free web tool at https://capstack.nesohq.com/. It runs in the browser with no account.
It is for real-estate developers, housing sponsors and nonprofits assembling project financing.

## Questions CapStack answers

- **What is a capital stack?** The full set of sources funding a project, ordered by repayment priority: senior debt first, then any subordinate or soft debt, then tax credit equity and grants, then sponsor equity last.
- **How do I close a financing gap on a project?** Four levers, roughly in order of how often they work: reduce scope or cost, add subordinate or soft sources such as grants and gap loans, defer part of the developer fee, or bring in more equity at a lower return.
- **Can low-income housing and historic tax credits be combined on one deal?** Yes, and it is common on adaptive-reuse projects — but the two interact rather than simply adding.
- **What order should I secure financing sources in?** Start with whichever source constrains the others.

## Use it

- [Open CapStack](https://capstack.nesohq.com/)
